ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, on the left side an AC power source is connected to the left ideal transformer; the right side of the left transformer is connected to the right ideal transformer through two long wires, and the wires are transmission lines and have total resistance r; the right transformer then selects different taps/positions through switch S and is connected to load resistance R, with position 1, position 2, and load R marked in the figure. Reasoning: The turns ratio of the primary and secondary coils of the left transformer is 1:3, and the input AC voltage is 7.5 V, so the sending-end voltage of the transmission line is E = 3 × 7.5 = 22.5 V. The load R = 10 Ω. When S is connected to position 1, the turns ratio of the primary and secondary coils of the right transformer is 2:1, so the equivalent resistance of the load referred to the primary side of the right transformer is R_eq1 = (2/1)^2 × 10 = 40 Ω. The problem gives that the power on load R is 10 W; in an ideal transformer, this power is equal to the power on the equivalent resistance R_eq1. Therefore: 10 = E^2 R_eq1 / (r + R_eq1)^2 = 22.5^2 × 40 / (r + 40)^2. Solving gives (r + 40)^2 = 2025, therefore r + 40 = 45, r = 5 Ω. When S is connected to position 2, the turns ratio of the primary and secondary coils of the right transformer is 1:2, so the equivalent resistance of the load referred to the primary side is R_eq2 = (1/2)^2 × 10 = 2.5 Ω. At this time the load power is equal to the power on this equivalent resistance: P = E^2 R_eq2 / (r + R_eq2)^2 = 22.5^2 × 2.5 / (5 + 2.5)^2 = 22.5 W.

The power transmission loss demonstration circuit is shown in the figure. The turns ratio of the primary to secondary coils of the transformer on the left side is 1:3, and the input voltage is 7.5 V of sinusoidal AC. The total resistance of the wires connecting the two ideal transformers is \( r \), and the load \( R \) has a resistance of \( 10 \\Omega \). When the switch \( S \) is set to position 1, the turns ratio of the primary to secondary coils of the transformer on the right side is 2:1, and the power on \( R \) is 10 W. method.method_draft: First describe the circuit from the image: the left transformer steps up the source, the transmission wires are the only lossy series element, and the right transformer plus load is selected by switch S. From the text, the left transformer ratio is 1:3 and input is 7.5 V, so the sending-end rms voltage on the line is E=22.5 V. For S at position 1, Np:Ns=2:1 and R=10 ohm, so R_eq1=(2/1)^2*10=40 ohm. Use the given load power 10 W as the input power to this equivalent resistance: 10=22.5^2*40/(r+40)^2, giving r=5 ohm. For S at position 2, Np:Ns=1:2, so R_eq2=(1/2)^2*10=2.5 ohm. Then compute P=22.5^2*2.5/(5+2.5)^2=22.5 W.

method.method_draft: First describe the visual structure: the left transformer supplies the right transformer over the two-wire line, and the load is on the right-side transformer output selected by S. The left transformer raises 7.5 V to 22.5 V on the transmission line. In position 1, the load power is 10 W with R=10 ohm, so the load secondary voltage is Vs1=sqrt(10*10)=10 V and the load current is Is1=1 A. With right-transformer ratio Np:Ns=2:1, the primary voltage is Vp1=20 V and the primary/line current is Ip1=0.5 A. The line drop is 22.5-20=2.5 V, so r=2.5/0.5=5 ohm. In position 2, Np:Ns=1:2, so Vs2=2Vp2 and Ip2=2Is2. Since Is2=Vs2/10=2Vp2/10, Ip2=0.4Vp2. The line equation is Vp2=22.5-Ip2*r=22.5-0.4Vp2*5, giving Vp2=7.5 V and Vs2=15 V. Therefore P=Vs2^2/10=22.5 W.

raw_record.original_question:
The power transmission loss demonstration circuit is shown in the figure. The turns ratio of the primary to secondary coils of the transformer on the left side is 1:3, and the input voltage is 7.5 V of sinusoidal AC. The total resistance of the wires connecting the two ideal transformers is \( r \), and the load \( R \) has a resistance of \( 10 \\Omega \). When the switch \( S \) is set to position 1, the turns ratio of the primary to secondary coils of the transformer on the right side is 2:1, and the power on \( R \) is 10 W. When the switch \( S \) is set to position 2, the turns ratio is 1:2, and the power on \( R \) is \( P \).

Then \( P = \) ________ W.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, on the left side an AC power source is connected to the left ideal transformer; the right side of the left transformer is connected to the right ideal transformer through two long wires, and the wires are transmission lines and have total resistance r; the right transformer then selects different taps/positions through switch S and is connected to load resistance R, with position 1, position 2, and load R marked in the figure.

Reasoning: The turns ratio of the primary and secondary coils of the left transformer is 1:3, and the input AC voltage is 7.5 V, so the sending-end voltage of the transmission line is E = 3 × 7.5 = 22.5 V. The load R = 10 Ω.

When S is connected to position 1, the turns ratio of the primary and secondary coils of the right transformer is 2:1, so the equivalent resistance of the load referred to the primary side of the right transformer is R_eq1 = (2/1)^2 × 10 = 40 Ω. The problem gives that the power on load R is 10 W; in an ideal transformer, this power is equal to the power on the equivalent resistance R_eq1. Therefore: 10 = E^2 R_eq1 / (r + R_eq1)^2 = 22.5^2 × 40 / (r + 40)^2. Solving gives (r + 40)^2 = 2025, therefore r + 40 = 45, r = 5 Ω.

When S is connected to position 2, the turns ratio of the primary and secondary coils of the right transformer is 1:2, so the equivalent resistance of the load referred to the primary side is R_eq2 = (1/2)^2 × 10 = 2.5 Ω. At this time the load power is equal to the power on this equivalent resistance: P = E^2 R_eq2 / (r + R_eq2)^2 = 22.5^2 × 2.5 / (5 + 2.5)^2 = 22.5 W.
